'''Josh Selby''' (born March 27, 1991 in [[Baltimore]], [[Maryland]]) is an [[United States|American]] basketball player who was a freshman on the [[2010–11 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team]].<ref>[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2010/apr/17/josh-selby-chooses-kansas/ Josh Selby chooses Kansas]</ref> Selby has declared his intention to enter the [[2011 NBA Draft]].

==High school & recruitment==
Selby attended [[Lake Clifton/Eastern High School|Lake Clifton High School]] in Baltimore for his senior year, having previously attended [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] in Hyattsville, MD and [[The John Carroll School]] in Bel Air, MD. He averaged 32 points, 7 assists, 5 rebounds, and two steals per game during his senior season.<ref>[http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041810aaa.html Kansas Men's Basketball Signs Standout Guard Josh Selby to National Letter of Intent]</ref>

Selby originally committed to play for the [[University of Tennessee]] but decommitted in July 2009.<ref>[http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/story/11969210 Top 10 recruit Selby withdraws commitment to Tennessee]</ref> On April 17, 2010 Selby committed to the [[University of Kansas|Kansas]] [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Jayhawks]] at the [[2010 Jordan Brand Classic]] at [[Madison Square Garden]] live on [[ESPN2]]. Selby picked the Jayhawks over a final list of teams including [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]], [[University of Connecticut|UConn]], [[University of Arizona|Arizona]] and Tennessee. Selby is the highest rated player ever signed by Kansas coach [[Bill Self]]<ref>[http://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/big12/2010-04-19-kansas-selby_N.htm Guard Josh Selby signs letter of intent with Kansas]</ref> as he was the #1 rated recruit on the recruiting website [[Rivals.com]].<ref>[http://kansas.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=1079783 Selby Takes #1 Spot in Final Rivals150]</ref>

He was named a [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010 McDonald's All-American]] and scored 12 points for the West team in the game.<ref>[http://www.mcdonaldsallamerican.com/2010_AAG_mens_results.html#GAME.BOX 2010 McDonald's All-American Game box score]</ref> Selby was also the winner of the dunk contest before the game.<ref>[http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2010-03-30/sports/bal-selby0330_1_dunk-contest-high-flying-act-all-american Lake Clifton's Josh Selby wins national slam dunk contest]</ref>

==College==
On December 18, 2010, following a nine-game suspension Selby joined  the [[2010–11 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2010-11 Jayhawks]] where he scored 21 points in 27 minutes and made a game winning shot.<ref name=SelbyDec18>{{Cite news |url=http://www2.kusports.com/weblogs/keegan_ratings/2010/dec/18/josh-selby-lives-up-to-hy/ |title=Josh Selby lives up to hype in opener }}</ref> While Selby sat out, Kansas led the country in many team statistical categories.{{Fact|Reason=not in dispute, just need a citation|date=March 2011}}. As a result of his suspension and later injuries Selby played in only 26 of the teams 38 games and averaged only 14 minutes per game after returning from injury. For the season he averaged 7.9 points and 2.2 assists on 20.4 minutes per game.

===Controversy===
After choosing to attend Kansas, a report came out stating that Selby had not yet been cleared to play by the [[NCAA]].<ref>[http://www.kansascity.com/2010/08/05/2131501/kus-josh-selby-reportedly-hasnt.html/ KU's Josh Selby reportedly hasn't been cleared by NCAA for basketball]</ref> According to this report, the NCAA had been investigating for months the relationship between Selby and Robert "Bay" Frazier, who is the business manager for [[New York Knicks]] star [[Carmelo Anthony]]. Selby had acknowledged a friendship with Anthony in past interviews and spoke of his contact with Frazier in an April story in [[The New York Times]]. All three are [[Baltimore]] natives. Maeshon Witherspoon, Selby's mother, told The Times that she had known Bay since elementary school and had asked him to serve the role of an adviser during his college recruitment.<ref>[http://www.nytimes.com/2010/04/17/sports/ncaabasketball/17hoops.html Colleges Wait to Hear Their Name Called by Elite Recruit]</ref> The Times report said Witherspoon asked Frazier to host Selby's in-home visits with college coaches at his own home and that Frazier attended a KU-Missouri game at [[Allen Fieldhouse]] in January 2009.

On November 21, 2010, the NCAA made their final ruling on the matter, suspending Selby for nine games, and ordering him to pay $4,607.58, the total of the "improper benefits" received, to the charity of his choice.<ref>[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=5827821/ NCAA rules Kansas freshman Josh Selby can play in December]</ref>

==Professional==
On April 14th, 2011 Selby announced via Twitter that he would enter his name in the [[2011 NBA Draft]]<ref>[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2011/apr/14/ku-freshman-josh-selby-will-not-return-next-season/ Josh Selby bids KU adieu]</ref>
